title: 'The Fall of the House of Usher,' by Edgar Allan Poe, Part Two
titleZh: 爱伦·坡的《厄舍屋的倒塌》第二部分

sentences.en: Roderick Usher, whom I had known as a boy, was now ill and had asked me to come to help him.
sentences.zh: Roderick Usher，我自幼便认识他，如今却病倒了，并请我来帮助他。

sentences.en: When I arrived I felt something strange and fearful about the great old stone house, about the lake in front of it, and about Usher himself.
sentences.zh: 当我抵达时，我对那座古老的大石屋、屋前的湖泊，以及Usher本人，都感到一种奇异而令人恐惧的气息。

sentences.en: He appeared not like a human being, but like a spirit that had come back from beyond the grave.
sentences.zh: 他看起来不像活人，倒像一个从坟墓之外归来的亡魂。

sentences.en: It was an illness, he said, from which he would surely die.
sentences.zh: 他说，这是一种绝症，他定会因此丧命。

sentences.en: He called his sickness fear.
sentences.zh: 他把自己的病称为“恐惧”。

sentences.en: “I have,” he said, “no fear of pain, but only the fear of its result — of terror.
sentences.zh: “我，”他说，“并不惧怕痛苦，只惧怕它的后果——那恐怖。

sentences.en: I feel that the time will soon arrive when I must lose my life, and my mind, and my soul, together, in some last battle with that horrible enemy: fear!”
sentences.zh: 我感到，时候很快就要到了，届时我将在与那可怕的敌人的最后一场搏斗中，连同我的生命、我的心智、我的灵魂，一起丧失——那敌人就是：恐惧！”

sentences.en: I learned also, but slowly, and through broken words with doubtful meaning, another strange fact about the condition of Usher’s mind.
sentences.zh: 我还了解到另一件关于Usher心智状况的奇异事实，但了解得很慢，是通过那些含义可疑的只言片语。

sentences.en: He had certain sick fears about the house in which he lived, and he had not stepped out of it for many years.
sentences.zh: 他对所居住的房屋怀有种种病态的恐惧，而且他已经多年没有踏出过那所房子。

sentences.en: He felt that the house, with its gray walls and the quiet lake around it, had somehow through the long years gotten a strong hold on his spirit.
sentences.zh: 他觉得，那座灰墙之屋和环绕它的静谧湖水，不知怎的，在漫长的岁月中，对他的灵魂攫取了一种强大的支配。

sentences.en: He said, however, that much of the gloom which lay so heavily on him was probably caused by something more plainly to be seen — by the long-continued illness — indeed, the coming death — of a dearly loved sister — his only company for many years.
sentences.zh: 不过他说，压在他身上、如此沉重的忧郁，很可能另有更显而易见的原因——那长期不愈的病症—— indeed，那即将到来的死亡——一位深爱的妹妹的死亡，她多年来是他唯一的伴侣。

sentences.en: Except for himself, she was the last member of his family on earth.
sentences.zh: 除了他自己，她是这世上家族中最后一位成员。

sentences.en: “When she dies,” he said, with a sadness which I can never forget, “when she dies, I will be the last of the old, old family — the House of Usher.”
sentences.zh: “当她死去，”他说，带着一种我永不能忘的悲伤，“当她死去，我将是那古老家族——Usher家族——最后的传人。”

sentences.en: While he spoke, the lady Madeline (for so she was called) passed slowly through a distant part of the room, and without seeing that I was there, went on.
sentences.zh: 当他说话时，那位名叫Madeline的女士（她正是如此被称呼）缓缓经过房间远处的一处，没有看见我在此，便继续前行。

sentences.en: I looked at her with a complete and wondering surprise and with some fear — and yet I found I could not explain to myself such feelings.
sentences.zh: 我以一种全然而惊异的目光注视着她，并带着几分恐惧——然而，我却无法向自己解释这样的感受。

sentences.en: My eyes followed her.
sentences.zh: 我的目光追随着她。

sentences.en: When she came to a door and it closed behind her, my eyes turned to the face of her brother — but he had put his face in his hands, and I could see only that the thin fingers through which his tears were flowing were whiter than ever before.
sentences.zh: 当她走到一扇门前、门在她身后关上时，我的目光转向了她哥哥的脸——但他已把脸埋进双手，我只能看见那泪水流淌的纤细手指，比以往任何时候都要苍白。

sentences.en: The illness of the lady Madeline had long been beyond the help of her doctors.
sentences.zh: Madeline女士的病症早已超出了她医生们所能救治的范围。

sentences.en: She seemed to care about nothing.
sentences.zh: 她似乎对什么都不在意。

sentences.en: Slowly her body had grown thin and weak, and often for a short period she would fall into a sleep like the sleep of the dead.
sentences.zh: 她的身体缓慢地变得消瘦而虚弱，常常有一小段时间，她会陷入一种类似死眠的沉睡。

sentences.en: So far she had not been forced to stay in bed; but by the evening of the day I arrived at the house, the power of her destroyer (as her brother told me that night) was too strong for her.
sentences.zh: 迄今为止，她尚未被要求卧床不起；然而就在我抵达那所房子的当天傍晚，她那位“毁灭者”（她哥哥当晚如此告诉我）的力量已强大到令她无法支撑。

sentences.en: I learned that my one sight of her would probably be the last I would have — that the lady, at least while living, would be seen by me no more.
sentences.zh: 我得知，我所见到的她的那一面，或许便是我最后一次见到她——那位女士，至少在她活着的时候，我将再也无法见到。

sentences.en: For several days following, her name was not spoken by either Usher or myself; and during this period I was busy with efforts to lift my friend out of his sadness and gloom.
sentences.zh: 在此后的数日里，无论是乌舍尔还是我，都不曾提起她的名字；而在这段时期，我忙于种种努力，试图将我的朋友从悲伤与阴郁中拯救出来。

sentences.en: We painted and read together; or listened, as if in a dream, to the wild music he played.
sentences.zh: 我们一同作画、读书；或如坠梦境般聆听他演奏的狂野音乐。

sentences.en: And so, as a warmer and more loving friendship grew between us, I saw more clearly the uselessness of all attempts to bring happiness to a mind from which only darkness came, spreading upon all objects in the world its never-ending gloom.
sentences.zh: 于是，随着我们之间日益温暖、愈发亲密的友谊不断加深，我愈发清楚地认识到，一切试图为那颗只被黑暗笼罩、并将无尽阴郁蔓延至世间万物的心灵带来幸福，都是徒劳的。

sentences.en: I shall always remember the hours I spent with the master of the House of Usher.
sentences.zh: 我将永远记得与那所“乌舍尔之家”的主人共度的时光。

sentences.en: Yet I would fail in any attempt to give an idea of the true character of the things we did together.
sentences.zh: 然而，若我试图用言语描绘我们一同所做之事的真实性情，必将失败。

sentences.en: There was a strange light over everything.
sentences.zh: 一种奇异的光笼罩着一切。

sentences.en: The paintings which he made me tremble, though I know not why.
sentences.zh: 那些画作令我浑身战栗，尽管我不知为何。

sentences.en: To tell of them is beyond the power of written words.
sentences.zh: 述说它们，非文字所能企及。

sentences.en: If ever a man painted an idea, that man was Roderick Usher.
sentences.zh: 若说曾有人画出了某种理念，那人便是罗德里克·乌舍尔。

sentences.en: For me at least there came out of his pictures a sense of fear and wonder.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，至少从他的画中流露出一种恐惧与惊奇之感。

sentences.en: One of these pictures may be told, although weakly, in words.
sentences.zh: 其中一幅画，或许能用言语勉强道出。

sentences.en: It showed the inside of a room where the dead might be placed, with low walls, white and plain.
sentences.zh: 它描绘了一间或许用于停放亡者的房间内部，墙壁低矮，洁白而素朴。

sentences.en: It seemed to be very deep under the earth.
sentences.zh: 它似乎深埋于地下极深处。

sentences.en: There was no door, no window; and no light or fire burned; yet a river of light flowed through it, filling it with a horrible, ghastly brightness.
sentences.zh: 那里没有门，没有窗；也没有灯火燃烧；然而一束光之河在其中流淌，将它填满，呈现出一种可怖的、惨白的光亮。

sentences.en: I have spoken of that sickly condition of the senses, which made most music painful for Usher to hear.
sentences.zh: 我已谈及那种病态的感官状态，正是它使大多数音乐令乌舍尔听来感到痛苦。

sentences.en: The notes he could listen to with pleasure were very few.
sentences.zh: 他能愉悦聆听的音符寥寥无几。

sentences.en: It was this fact, perhaps, that made the music he played so different from most music.
sentences.zh: 或许正是这一事实，使他所演奏的音乐与大多数音乐大相径庭。

sentences.en: But the wild beauty of his playing could not be explained.
sentences.zh: 然而，他演奏中那种狂野之美，却无法加以解释。

sentences.en: The words of one of his songs, called “The Haunted Palace,” I have easily remembered.
sentences.zh: 他一首歌里的歌词，名为“幽闭的宫殿”，我很容易就记住了。

sentences.en: In it I thought I saw, and for the first time, that Usher knew very well that his mind was weakening.
sentences.zh: 在其中，我仿佛看到，也是头一回，夏特清楚地知道他的精神正在衰退。

sentences.en: This song told of a great house where a king lived — a palace — in a green valley, where all was light and color and beauty, and the air was sweet.
sentences.zh: 这首歌讲述了一座宏伟的宅邸，一位国王居住其中——一座宫殿——坐落在一片翠绿的山谷里，那里充满光明、色彩与美丽，空气也格外甜美。

sentences.en: In the palace were two bright windows through which people in that happy valley could hear music and could see smiling ghosts — spirits — moving around the king.
sentences.zh: 宫殿里有两扇明亮的窗户，山谷中的人们透过窗户就能听到音乐，还能看到微笑的幽灵——灵魂——在国王身边徘徊。

sentences.en: The palace door was of the richest materials, in red and white; through it came other spirits whose only duty was to sing in their beautiful voices about how wise their king was.
sentences.zh: 宫殿的大门由最华贵的材料制成，红白相间；透过大门，其他灵魂涌来，它们唯一的职责就是用优美的嗓音歌唱，赞颂国王是如何的睿智。

sentences.en: But a dark change came, the song continued, and now those who enter the valley see through the windows, in a red light, shapes that move to broken music; while through the door, now colorless, a ghastly river of ghosts, laughing but no longer smiling, rushes out forever.
sentences.zh: 然而，一种黑暗的转变悄然降临，歌曲继续唱道，如今踏入山谷的人们透过窗户，在红色的光晕中，看到随破碎旋律舞动的形体；而透过那扇如今失去色彩的大门，一股阴森的幽灵之河，笑着却不再微笑，永远地奔涌而出。

sentences.en: Our talk of this song led to another strange idea in Usher’s mind.
sentences.zh: 我们关于这首歌的交谈，引来了夏特脑海中另一个奇怪的想法。

sentences.en: He believed that plants could feel and think, and not only plants, but rocks and water as well.
sentences.zh: 他相信植物能够感知和思考，不仅植物如此，连岩石和水也是如此。

sentences.en: He believed that the gray stones of his house, and the small plants growing on the stones, and the decaying trees, had a power over him that made him what he was.
sentences.zh: 他相信他宅邸里那些灰色的石头，石头上生长的小小植物，以及那些腐朽的树木，都拥有一种左右他的力量，才使他成了如今这般模样。

sentences.en: Our books — the books which, for years, had fed the sick man’s mind — were, as might be supposed, of this same wild character.
sentences.zh: 我们的书籍——这些多年来滋养着这位病人的心灵的书籍——正如人们可以料想的那样，也是同样狂野的性质。

sentences.en: Some of these books Usher sat and studied for hours.
sentences.zh: 其中有些书，夏特会坐下来，一研究就是好几个小时。

sentences.en: His chief delight was found in reading one very old book, written for some forgotten church, telling of the Watch over the Dead.
sentences.zh: 他主要的乐趣在于阅读一本极其古老的书籍，那是为某个被遗忘的教会所写，讲述“亡者守望者”的故事。

sentences.en: At last, one evening he told me that the lady Madeline was alive no more.
sentences.zh: 最后，一天傍晚，他告诉我，那位女士玛德琳已经不再活着了。

sentences.en: He said he was going to keep her body for a time in one of the many vaults inside the walls of the building.
sentences.zh: 他说，他打算把她的遗体暂时保存在建筑内部众多墓穴中的一个。

sentences.en: The worldly reason he gave for this was one with which I felt I had to agree.
sentences.zh: 他为此给出的世俗理由，是我不得不认同的。

sentences.en: He had decided to do this because of the nature of her illness, because of the strange interest and questions of her doctors, and because of the great distance to the graveyard where members of his family were placed in the earth.
sentences.zh: 他之所以决定这么做，是因为她病情的性质，是因为她医生们奇异的关注与疑问，也是因为埋葬他家族成员的墓地距离太远。

sentences.en: We two carried her body to its resting place.
sentences.zh: 我们两人将她的遗体抬到了安息之所。

sentences.en: The vault in which we placed it was small and dark, and in ages past it must have seen strange and bloody scenes.
sentences.zh: 我们安放她的那个墓穴又小又暗，在遥远的过去，它一定见证过奇异而血腥的场景。

sentences.en: It lay deep below that part of the building where I myself slept.
sentences.zh: 它深埋在我本人所睡的那部分建筑之下。

sentences.en: The thick door was of iron, and because of its great weight made a loud, hard sound when it was opened and closed.
sentences.zh: 厚重的门是铁制的，由于分量极重，开合时会发出响亮而坚硬的声音。

sentences.en: As we placed the lady Madeline in this room of horror I saw for the first time the great likeness between brother and sister, and Usher told me then that they were twins — they had been born on the same day.
sentences.zh: 当我们把玛德琳女士安置在这间恐怖房间里时，我第一次看到了兄妹之间惊人的相似，拉斯特当时告诉我，他们是双胞胎——在同一天出生的。

sentences.en: For that reason the understanding between them had always been great, and the tie that held them together very strong.
sentences.zh: 正因为如此，他们之间的默契一直很深，维系他们之间的情感纽带也非常牢固。

sentences.en: We looked down at the dead face one last time, and I was filled with wonder.
sentences.zh: 我们最后一次俯视那张苍白的面孔，我心中充满了惊奇。

sentences.en: As she lay there, the lady Madeline looked not dead but asleep — still soft and warm — though to the touch cold as the stones around us.
sentences.zh: 当她躺在那里时，玛德琳女士看起来不像死去，而像是睡着了——依然柔软而温暖——尽管触摸起来却像我们周围的石头一样冰冷。

glossary.def: a hole in the ground for burying a dead body
to shake slightly because you are afraid, nervous, or excited
the official home of a king, queen, president, or other official
the soul of a dead person thought of as living in an unseen world or as appearing to living people
a building that is used for Christian religious services
a locked room where money or valuable things are kept
a place where people are buried; cemetery
a very strong feeling of fear, dread, and shock
